title: Better service
text: I’ve been using the app instagram for as long as I can remember. I can say that it is a part of me in a good way. I haven’t always followed the rules but for the most part being on the app was a great experience. As someone with a growing platform and growing instagram account, I can say that when you are in need of some help there’s not really anyone to call on. The email and number are from my experience never used, which makes both ways to contact them pointless. But another thing is is the biometric identification bot, is an obstacle to pass. I recently have been trying to access my account and it’s been a nightmare. So likewise I’ve been searching and watching online videos and reading sources on how to pass the “obstacle”. I feel like human review should be put to use more simply because it’s hard for an ai to understand something less perplexed. I think the ai  wants you to be perfect which is going to be hard for a lot of people. Currently writing this review I have not gotten fully into my account due to the 2fa which is the start of the problem, but hopefully I can get back into my account this week.  In conclusion, the app is great but there are some things that needs to be worked on and changed. For example the identification verification bot and a little more but that’s all. A tip before I finish is to get your 8 digit codes because those will be a life saver (while you have access to your account).

title: Maintenance
text: I have had a frustrating issue for several months now where certain features either make the app crash suddenly, or do not work entirely. One feature that does not work at all. Not a single time... is the ability to post multiple photos in a singular post. I’ve tried with just 2 photos. I’ve tried with the maximum amount of photos in a photoset(10). Not a single time has this worked. After adding a caption with some hashtags, tagging friends, and waiting for the post to load. It fails to post every single time. I’ve tried this on both my old phone iPhone 6S plus, as well as my most recent phone purchase the iPhone X. This feature has never worked for me, often times being so frustrated I’d neglect the app for a few days and then find myself back. After attempting to delete the app as well as the app cache and reinstalling on both phones the feature is still inoperative. I also agree with many other Instagram users that the feed is very annoying that I’ll see posts I’ve seen already, or posts from several days ago. Chronological order?? If Instagram was more oriented on creating a seamless working application they may have a lot more users, or more frequent users of the app. Every bug I’ve experienced, I’ve submitted through the in app report a bug.

title: A DISGRACE
text: I have used this app almost every single day since 2014. I was 11. And I have loved it every step of the way. I’ve had very few issues with bugs and my feed has been curated perfectly towards me. However, this recent update is genuinely about to make me delete this app. The rectangles instead of squares on the feed is ridiculous and ugly. It messes up the whole feed and cuts out a quarter of the picture when looking at the feed itself. But that’s not even the main issue. When I go to my explore page now, I don’t even see regular posts. Used to, when I would go to my explore page, it would look just like my home page, but just show me things from people I don’t follow. Now, however. Any post I tap on on the explore page, automatically takes me to what looks like “reels” but it’s NOT reels. They are normal posts. These memes I’m seeing, half the words are cut off, because it was meant to be viewed in a normal post, and not in a reel post. title: Newest update?
text:
I love Instagram, it’s my go-to social media and it’s the one I’m most comfortable using. However, this morning after updating, certain posts refuse to load, and most of them are the most recent posts on some of my favorite accounts. Videos are struggling to load and buffer way more than usual. I’ve tried closing the app and reopening it, going to the post on the account and trying to refresh it, whatever you can think of, and it’s not working.
Also I am not a fan of the new profile layout. I have a couple different accounts and each of them seems to have one of three different layouts and it really bothers me. 
I preferred when it was normal, and you had your post/follower/following count across the top, then the edit profile below that, your account description, stories, and then the post overview/scrolling/tagged photos option across the bottom.
Now on some of my accounts, you have to tap on a post in the overview in order to scroll through your posts, and you can’t see just one post at a time. I don’t like it. If I wanted to scroll through them I would have used the scrolling option. When I tap on a photo in the overview I want to just see that post. There also seems to be a waste of blank space on the profile, which is for stories I’m sure, but I’m not posting stories so it should just collapse down and not waste space on my profile.
I do still love the app, and it’s not like I’m going to stop using it now after all these years, but these are just some new things that have come up and I’m not a fan at all.

title: New to Internet & Instagram
text: I am a product of the ‘60s, very familiar with phone usage, but still learning how this “iphone”and all its apps., & “collection of information” operates,(in the day of “landlines” & “party lines”, this was considered eavesdropping or wiretapping). But having nothing to hide & hiding nothing, I will try to move into the 21st century, while trying not to think of this “phone”as a tool for “Big Brother”. Anyway, since this is handy to keep in touch with family, that is busy and has only spare minutes to communicate, I will get in line with the rest of the #s. I have only one comment(maybe two); the collection of information of “our investigations”, say on Google for instance, or Wikipedia, or a medical source, does not necessarily reflect our own health. It truly can be curiosity, or an intellectual search to increase knowledge, much like “going to the library”. By trying to tie all researches into one picture you are making a one-dimensional assumption. Even for ads/sale/promos, you call “cookies”, do you remember Pinterest? “Wishbook” daydreaming ! The “iPhone” practicality WAS good as an extension of being part of the community wherever we may be, but it’s becoming weary with all the 🔍🗿intrusive stipulations and assumptions. Truthfully, I feel like I am training a robot just to use the text with all of it’s challenges and having to correct “her/Siri “. You’ve heard my “computer-illiterate “ review, and I’m going back to writing ✍️ letters! Thank you for asking!

title: Hiding story views and comments
text:
Not sure what’s going on with this app or my account, but over the past 48 hours or so I’ve noticed 2 issues:
1) Instagram doesn’t show you the total number of people who viewed your story. I had a follower in my DMs who replied to a story I posted, but when I looked at who viewed my story, this follower didn’t show up in the list of viewers. Also, I had a story posted 10 minutes after the previous story I posted, & the discrepancy in views was large—the story posted 10 minutes later had 60% less views that the story before it. And they were only posted 10 minutes apart. It doesn’t make any sense unless Instagram was intentionally hiding the story from my followers. A story posted 10 minutes later should have about the same number of views as the previous story, not 60% less views.
2) The second issue: I opened up instagram this morning & started scrolling and every time I clicked a post to view the comments it said “no comments” even though there were hundreds / thousands of comments under the posts. I tried deleting & reinstalling the app & it still said “no comments” each time I clicked on a post with hundreds of comments. 

I reported both issues to Instagram support, but I don’t know if anything actually gets done about it.

title: Latest update
text: With each update, for however long, IG has gotten more and more uncomfortable to engage with. And this latest one just about ignores readability with how captions are handled for posts. If a thing isn’t broke why try to fix it - especially when there is truly no actual improvement. I really loathe engaging my feed at this point. If I wanted something that looked and behaved like any other app - I’d go on and use that app instead. I don’t need (or want!) IG to be anything other than IG with all of the ease of use that used to be there. At the very least give people an option to simplify things rather than rearranging buttons and stuff. What’s the point of doing polls/surveys when the needs of the people aren’t really being addressed? Make it make sense!

title: Algorithm, stories, and login/security need some work
text:
I’ve been on insta for quite a while, but I’ve noticed that some of the features (noticeably the ones that are also shared, or should I say dominated by other apps) need improvement.
1) Close friends stories. Why can I only have one? If the goal was to implement similar features to sn*pchat, then why can’t I have multiple close friends for different friend groups/family/business partners? It’s been years since this feature has been available on other apps and Meta has made no effort to improve upon it, opting instead for location mapping (which most don’t use due to larger following or public accounts) and Instagram notes (attention seeking).
2) Login/security. Why can I not connect my iCloud account to Meta and use it to log in? From anecdotes, many of my friends have had their instagrams hacked, but it seems like iCloud is generally harder for scammers to access…additionally, getting locked out of my Instagram accounts has happened to me more than once. Meta should consider implementing this feature like other social media apps have.
3) finally, the algorithm isn’t as good as other social media apps. Understandably some, including myself, may be concerned about the lack of privacy and the information Meta is obtaining. However, given how much information is already available to them upon making an account, I would expect higher quality content on reels and suggested posts than what I am currently seeing.
More than willing to adjust my review should I see these features implemented.

title: Creative and User-Enhancing Suggestions
text: Dear Instagram Developers, I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to offer a few suggestions that I believe would greatly benefit and enhance the functionality of Instagram. Secondly, I would like to address a concern regarding the white circle that surrounds the profile photo. In my opinion, this visual element can sometimes disrupt the overall aesthetic and proportion of the photo. I respectfully suggest that the option to remove or customize this circle be made available, allowing users to further curate their profiles in alignment with their personal branding. Last but not least, I would like to express my desire for Instagram to support the option of using GIFs as profile photos. This animated form of self-expression would undoubtedly inject a playful and engaging element into users' profiles, increasing their appeal and individuality. I genuinely believe that these proposals could positively impact the Instagram user experience, fostering increased creativity and allowing for further personalization. I appreciate your time and consideration, and I eagerly look forward to seeing the continued evolution of the platform. Thank you for your attention to these suggestions.

title: I’m case Systrom and his staff only read good reviews.
text:
Look Instagram is great, I find it very entertaining and go on it almost every day. But it is really hard for new artists like my friends and myself and even bigger artists to continue using it because of the algorithm that flops our accounts. I am aware that there is the whole idea where you should post often, but it gets very discouraging when you have to fight tooth and nail to get your post noticed and it doesn’t make sense that you earn all of these followers and only 10% active or inactive can see it. I have a friend artist who draws amazing realism and had nearly 5k followers and would get thousands of likes in her posts, but thanks to the algorithm she now only has 2,970 followers and on a good day gets 500 likes. I get that part of it has to do with people’s preferences but this proves that Instagram doesn’t appreciate their users hard work and talent that is put into their posts. 

Another downfall is that Instagram doesn’t allow people to take breaks from it for mental health, and because of that, it is even more frustrating to even try to use the app. How am I supposed to want to keep using Instagram if it doesn’t even promote mental and emotional wellness by allowing people to take breaks? If the Creators of Instagram appreciate their users and respect their well being, then they would revise this algorithm to give everyone a fair chance. I’m not saying that every artist or creator will make it big, but I am saying that maybe more artists will actually use Instagram if they knew they had a fair shot at success. We make up a fairly large percentage of people that use Instagram after all, I guess we’ll see if the creators really care about their users or not.

title: Useful, but too addictive and too messy
text: Instagram is pretty useful in some ways. Like, its good for messaging friends or following people I care about, and discovering new places or restaurants, that kind of thing. I keep up with creators and stuff too, so I keep it on my phone. Theres real value there, I think. But honestly, the app feels way too loaded up now. The feed used to be more about photos from the people I follow, but its turned into this endless stream of Reels and ads, plus all these suggested posts that the algorithm shoves at you. It makes it super easy to scroll for hours without even realizing. And then there are so many features piled on, Reels, Stories, Notes, even stuff like Threads or shopping recommendations, and notifications that never stop. That gets a bit messy for me. title: Taking Accounts Down Unnecessarily and Random Ads
text:
I have been using instagram for almost 3 years, and have made my way into the fandom side of Instagram lately. I have a fan account that is in danger of being reported and taken down. Lately, many people across fandoms have had their accounts taken down from other users reporting their accounts for impersonating YouTubers or celebrities. Instagram had the chance to review the accounts and made the decision to take the accounts down. They did nothing wrong and were not impersonating anyone. One of the accounts even had the words “fan page” in their bio. You need to hire better people to review the reports, or have actual people review them and not robots.
I also don’t like how there are more ads on the site. And most of them are scams. I’ve seen some good ads for real businesses, but a lot of the ads I’ve seen are just random companies promoting random things that don’t interest me. Those are the ads that annoy me the most. I have to scroll very far down just to see the accounts I want to see, and not accounts Instagram thinks I want to see. I’m usually very active on certain accounts, but I still don’t see enough posts from them. I have to have notifications on to actually see all the posts. 
Instagram is a great app though, aside from them taking down accounts and random promotions. I love the new layout, and the explore page is better than it was a few years ago, in my opinion. I do like the communities it creates. 
But, as a final analysis, I think that Instagram should have a better review team, and should target ads better and less often.

title: User Experience Addition Proposal
text:
Dear Instagram,
Your app is a great platform to engage with; each feature designed to engage audiences, be a marketing tool, and allow its users to fashion it as a creative portfolio, or just a place to connect and express. Despite all this, I believe, when it comes to the organization of the “Saved” section of one’s personal account, that it would benefit to have a search bar be added. This would allow a user to directly search the name of a saved folder when looking or saving the content. My belief of this comes from my personal user experience where I have often attempted to utilize Instagram in a way similar to Pinterest, saving videos and posts for later inspiration, projects, etc… but I find it a struggle todo so, as when I go to place it in a folder I have to scroll through each and every folder I have. This creates difficulty even when I am using the folder consistently. I believe that the platform allows people to showcase so many different ideas and expressions, but when one wants to save it for later, once it is saved they may never able to find it again, or it will takes painstakingly long todo so.

title: What happened to the app I loved?
text:

I’m served adds and content I didn’t follow and am constantly missing out on important updates from people I actually care about - the whole point of the app allowing me to specifically target my experience is gone, and Instagram frankly doesn’t care about its users as they are all the product themselves.

title: The algorithm is upsetting
text: Hi instagram! I enjoy your app with reels and such, but there are many aspects that make me want to bring my time and hard work to other apps. I am an artist, and I’m sure someone working at instagram by now has noticed how upset artists are with hashtags and how the algorithm works. We want a change so that us small artists can actually reach new followers. So far, the only way to do that is by using one audio that, by this point, everyone despises. Hashtags do not work to reach new people, and my feed doesn’t post from everyone I’m following. It chooses the same exact people to show me, and every once in awhile switches a few of them. Sometimes I refresh my feed, and it doesn’t even show me anything new. I’ve been on this platform for a long time now, and I can’t get my art out there no matter what I’m doing ! The same goes for so many amazingly talented artists, who all deserve the art to be seen. I understand that everyone wants clout and attention on this app, I also understand you can’t meet everyone’s demands all the time. We just ask that we can get a chance. At least, a chance at other people looking at our art depending on things such as hashtags. I have one reel awhile back that blew up, but it wasn’t even that good of a reel. The drawings were poor and only quickly sketched as a joke for the audio. The only reason that reel blew up was BECAUSE of the audio, and not the content. I have run across thousands of upset artists at this point, who are simply doing everything to appease the algorithm, and to no avail. I hope you take this into consideration, because at this point, you’re going to start losing people to other apps.

title: Too many bugs for its popularity
text:
I run an informational account so I try to post as much as I can. I have an old phone, maybe 3 or 4 years, but every other app works fine. Not instagram. About half of my posts, I am unable to post. It stays at the top of my screen with a message “unable to post. Try again later” with a reload button and an x button next to it. Occasionally I am able to end up posting the original, but most of the time I have to re-caption and post it again. No matter what I do, I am unable to change the outcome - whether I turn off my WiFi or keep it on. Either it will end up posting on its own or it will just stay up there until I delete it. 
With this problem, I am unable to see what I’ve posted or the caption and I am unable to save it to post it later - either I completely delete it or I hope that it might load eventually. 
If I log onto another phone, it does not show that I am trying to post these images. It also does not show that I have any saved posts that I am ready to post - it just disregards all of the work I have already put into my account. 
For such a popular app, I would expect this process to be much easier. I should be able to see what I posted if it isn’t able to post and I should be able to decide I want to post them later if they aren’t posting. I should also be able to see posts I have created but yet to post, given that they are saved through my Instagram account and not through my phone. 
These bugs honestly make me consider that it’s not worth using the app.

title: Don’t Be Too Active
text: I’ve been an Instagram user for 5+ years and have never run into an issue until I created a page in order to recommend shows. It’s a passion of mine so I decided to share that passion with likeminded people. I created the page, followed similar pages, and was very active within this niche community. The problems soon started as I tried to supper countless pages and their respective posts. Apparently, Instagram has it in their algorithm to limit the amount of actions a user can make over a given period of time. I understand that they’re trying to get rid of bots and clean up the app. However, it truly does active users a disservice by not only dictating the number of actions they can take, but also also banning them for exceeding this magic number. In that span of a month, I’ve been banned twice for unintentionally exceeding this tally, and placed on a week-long ban. Furthermore, it displays a message claiming that I used a third-party application in order to increase my following. What could be more insulting than questioning both my integrity and hardwork?! It’s absolutely astonishing to see this wildly successful app incapable of producing an algorithm that helps it differentiate between bot activity and an overly zealous Instagram user who wants to grow his page. I can help but be discouraged by this ban and it makes me question whether I want to continue using this application seeing the path it continues to travel down. To add insult to injury, when I tell them they’ve made a mistake in countless messages to the Help Center (which provides no help at all), I’m stuck in limbo waiting for a reply that will never come. It’s shocking to see. I expect more from Instagram , but a one-star rating still seems too kind given my treatment thus far.

title: Horrible algorithm took my following
text:
Back in 2018, my artwork went viral. In fact, many pieces went viral. People were finally starting to see my work all over the world. I was getting jobs and gaining so much traction! And that’s because both my following AND non followers could see my work. I eventually gained 93 thousand followers, getting my artwork to industry professionals. This was literally something I could put on my artistic resume. 
But then 2020 rolls around, and IG decides it wants to be just like another video app. Reels are on full blast. You now have to pay to get your posts to be seen by anyone, even your own followers. Less than 1% of my followers and non followers were even seeing my work. 93k, and interactions were tanked. Then… each week, without any real idea why- I was losing a thousand followers. I wasn’t doing anything different, but the following was drifting away. No one could see my art. Eventually I made a new IG and tried to get everyone over to that one, and then… I could never access that other page again. I go back and check it… it’s following swindled by over 30k. But I will never be able to access it again. I tried contacting IG to no luck. I proved myself the owner to no luck. Needless to say… this affected my jobs. 
The algorithm change screwed artists. We had to search for a new home, and there’s been nothing. Everything either has no traction or it has ai. Instagram screwed a huge chunk of its base.

title: Instagram Security Overreach Locks Out Legitimate Users -Time for Transparency
text:
Instagram’s recent security systems seem overly aggressive and opaque, leading to many legitimate users being unable to access their accounts for days with no clear explanation or resolution path. Reports from users across the U.S. indicate that thousands of people believe flaws in Meta’s automated security and moderation tools have led to false lockouts and account suspensions. According to a recent Boston 25 Now story, “thousands of Facebook and Instagram users believe a flaw in Meta’s security AI has led to false accusations and wrongful lockouts,” with users struggling to regain access and contact support effectively.  ￼

This problem is not isolated — widespread complaints, historic pressures from state attorneys general over takeovers and lockouts, and third-party reports about usability issues highlight systemic challenges. In fact, a 2024 letter from 40 state attorneys general to Meta called for “immediate action” to better prevent account takeovers and lockouts because consumer complaints had surged sharply.  ￼ Instagram and Meta need to improve their account recovery tools, transparency on how security decisions are made, and direct human support options so that users aren’t helpless when the automated systems mistakenly block them.
